title: Temporal Segmentation
description: Represent labelled time intervals within a media source, such as chapters, scenes, shots, speaker turns or detected events. Segments may overlap, may nest, and need not cover the whole source.

producer.description: The creator (model, tool or author) of these segments (e.g., 'PySceneDetect', 'pyannote', 'Manual Review').

track_id.description: (Optional) Identifier for the specific audio or video track in the source media. Numeric identifiers are written as strings (e.g., '0').

duration.description: The total duration of the source media in seconds. When present, no segment's end_time may exceed it.

vocabulary.description: A list of the possible segment labels. For more than 100 labels, use 'vocabulary_url'.

items.description: A single valid label from the vocabulary.

vocabulary_url.description: A URL pointing to a more detailed external vocabulary or ontology.

score_explanation.description: Defines the meaning of the 'score' field.

segments.description: The labelled time intervals. Can be empty if no segments were found.

id.description: An identifier for this segment (e.g., 'scene-12'). Must be unique within the record.

parent_id.description: The id of the segment that contains this one (e.g., the chapter containing a scene). Must be the id of another segment in the record, and this segment must lie within its parent's interval.

group_id.description: An identifier for the entity this segment belongs to. Segments sharing a group_id belong to the same entity (e.g., all turns of speaker 'SPEAKER_00'). Numeric identifiers, such as diarization cluster numbers, are written as strings (e.g., '0').

label.description: The category of the segment (e.g., 'chapter', 'scene', 'speaker', 'explosion'). Must be a member of 'vocabulary' when it is present.

title.description: A human-readable name for this segment (e.g., a chapter title).

description.description: A description of what happens in this segment.

start_time.description: Segment start time in seconds from the start of the source.

end_time.description: Segment end time in seconds from the start of the source. Must not be earlier than start_time; equal times mark an instantaneous event.

score.description: The confidence that the label applies to this interval, ranging from 0.0 (uncertain) to 1.0 (certain).

attributes.description: Arbitrary metadata relevant to this segment.
Arbitrary metadata relevant to this record (e.g., annotator, source, job ID).
